title: Validating Generative Virtual Patients for Intended Medical AI Uses: A Critical Narrative Review
content: Generative virtual patients (VPs) now support medical large language model training, interactive policy optimization, capability benchmarking, safety red-teaming, and clinical education. They are both evaluation objects and measurement instruments: source substrates, demographic distributions, and response policies shape training signals and evaluation conclusions. Their errors are not merely random noise; they may propagate as structured, configuration-dependent bias across the evidence-generation chain. Yet validation studies often assess script fidelity, fluency, inter-rater reliability, or case plausibility without testing how these measurements support downstream decisions. We synthesize evidence along a five-node chain: source substrate, patient information state and response policy, doctor–patient interaction, scoring and outcomes, and downstream decisions. Across this chain, local adequacy alone never licenses cross-setting extrapolation: disclosure policies determine which inquiry capabilities can be elicited, scoring reliability fails to guarantee construct validity, and case-level diagnostic coherence can coexist with population-level epidemiological distortion. Admission-time information loss and public-EHR case recall remain hypotheses requiring targeted audits, while simulated-user performance may fail to predict human interaction outcomes. Increasing the number of independent simulation runs reduces sampling variance but cannot resolve untested discrepancies from target clinical settings. We propose an intended-use validation framework that defines target estimands, tests decision-critical assumptions via paired temporal audits, clinically reviewed perturbations, and task-matched human references, and documents reuse boundaries in an Evaluation Provenance Statement. Before interactive evaluation standards solidify, validating specific simulator configurations for defined inferences—not VP technology in the abstract—is essential for credible medical AI training, benchmarking, governance, and algorithmovigilance.
